cards.text: David is laying low with his men, steering clear of Saul, Israel's king. Then a report comes in: "Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and looting the threshing floors." A whole town is under attack, and its harvest is getting carried off.

cards.question: A town is under attack, and David hears about it. Before he makes a move, what does he do first?

cards.text: David asks, "Should I go and attack these Philistines?" And the LORD says, "Go and attack the Philistines and save Keilah."

cards.question: God says go to Keilah, but David's men push back. They tell David they're already ___ right here in Judah.

cards.text: Their words: "Look, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?" That's me flinching at the oven timer, and somebody signs me up for SKYDIVING.

cards.question: With his men scared, David asks the LORD about Keilah a second time.
When David asks the LORD again about Keilah, what does the LORD promise him?

answers.text: He'll send a storm against them

cards.text: The LORD says, "Go at once to Keilah, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand." So David and his men march to Keilah, scared men and all, and they fight.

cards.question: At Keilah, just as the LORD promised, David and his men strike the Philistines with a ___ blow.

cards.text: David saves the people of Keilah, and he and his men carry off the Philistines' livestock. Quick side note: Abiathar son of Ahimelech, a priest who fled to David, brought something with him.

cards.question: When Abiathar the priest fled to David at Keilah, he brought the ___ with him.

cards.text: Now word reaches Saul that David went into Keilah. I bet Saul's grinning like a cat that just watched the mouse run into the CLOSET.

cards.question: Saul hears David is inside Keilah. Why does Saul think David has trapped himself?

cards.text: So Saul calls up ALL his troops to besiege Keilah and trap David and his men. When David learns Saul is plotting against him, he tells Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod."
Then David prays, "O LORD, God of Israel," and asks two things straight out. Will the citizens of Keilah surrender him into Saul's hand, and will Saul really come down?

cards.question: David asks the LORD whether Saul will really come down to Keilah. The LORD answers that Saul won't.
David asks again about the citizens of Keilah. The LORD says they will surrender David and his men into Saul's hand.

cards.text: He SAVED their town, and they'd still hand him over, which is like returning a stranger's lost wallet and getting reported for stealing it. So David and his men, about six hundred strong, leave Keilah and keep moving from place to place.

cards.question: Saul hears that David has escaped from Keilah. What does Saul do?

cards.text: David settles into the wilderness strongholds in the hill country of Ziph. And day after day, Saul searches for him.

cards.question: Day after day Saul searches for David, but ___ would not deliver David into his hand.

cards.text: David's in Horesh, in the Wilderness of Ziph, and he sees Saul has come out to take his life. Then a visitor shows up, and friend, it is NOT Saul.

cards.question: A visitor comes to David in Horesh while Saul is out hunting him. Who is it?

cards.text: Jonathan strengthens David's hand in God, the king's own son walking into the wilderness to encourage the man his dad is hunting. That is a FRIEND, friend.

cards.question: Jonathan tells David not to be afraid. What does Jonathan say about his father Saul?

answers.text: Saul will never lay a hand on him
Saul will make him a commander

cards.question: Jonathan keeps encouraging David. What does Jonathan say about David's future?
Jonathan says that when David is king, Jonathan will be his second-in-command.
Jonathan tells David that even his father Saul knows David will be king.
Before Jonathan heads home, he and David make a ___ before the LORD.

cards.text: Jonathan goes home, and David stays in Horesh. Then the Ziphites, the people of Ziph, go up to Saul at Gibeah.

cards.question: The Ziphites tell Saul at Gibeah that David is ___ among them in the strongholds at Horesh.

cards.text: The Ziphites offer to hand David over whenever Saul wants. Saul answers, "May you be blessed by the LORD," and says they've had compassion on him, which is a LOT of sympathy for the guy with the army.

cards.question: Saul's been told David is extremely cunning. So what does Saul ask the Ziphites to do?

cards.text: The Ziphites head to Ziph ahead of Saul. By now David and his men are in the Wilderness of Maon, and Saul and his men go looking for him.

cards.question: When David is told Saul is coming, he leaves the Wilderness of Maon.

cards.text: David goes down to the rock, and Saul chases him there. Saul's on one side of the mountain, David and his men are on the other, David's hurrying to get away, and Saul's CLOSING IN.

cards.question: Saul and his men are closing in to capture David. Then what happens?

answers.text: A messenger brings news of a raid
David's men turn and fight back
A storm stops Saul's whole army

cards.question: The messenger tells Saul the Philistines have raided the land. So Saul breaks off chasing David and goes to meet the Philistines.

cards.text: That spot gets a name, Sela-hammahlekoth, and I dare you to say it three times fast. Then David goes up and lives in the strongholds of En-gedi, and hang onto your apron, friend, because we are nowhere near the last page.

findings.problem: This blank asks for the unseen adjective 'mighty.' The earlier cards say only that David and his men fight, giving no battle detail from which the baker can reason out that wording rather than another plausible description such as 'single.' It tests the verse's wording instead of an inferable meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The retelling of verse 7 omits Saul's claim that God has delivered David into his hand, and no later card supplies it. This is an important part of Saul's response and contrasts with verse 14, where God would not deliver David into Saul's hand.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Verse 10's report that Saul intends to destroy Keilah on David's account is omitted here and never covered later. David's concern for the city is an important part of his prayer and of the danger facing Keilah.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The wrong answers are not reliably false. Jonathan strengthens David and makes a covenant with him later in this passage, so a baker could reasonably argue that Jonathan also would not deliver David into Saul's hand. Abiathar is likewise presented as David's ally, not as someone who would betray him.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The correct answer, 'Find all his hiding places,' comes from verse 23. Verse 22 supplies the question's setup about David's cunning but is not a verse of the right answer, so the citation should be 1 Samuel 23:23 rather than 1 Samuel 23:22-23.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.
